reason: All four rules state what is wrong: 083 says the delivered code includes unrequested features and speculative abstractions; 206 says the agent responds to a fix request with unrelated changes or superficial substitutes; 296 says behavior changes are smuggled into a refactor; 298 says the agent edits code unrelated to the current task. Each rule names a concrete failure in which the delivered change exceeds the requested scope.

All three rules measure size and flag a number without determining whether the growth traces to the request. Rule 107 scores complexity times net LOC growth over a time window. Rule 204 flags any positive non-test LOC delta from git numstat. Rule 483 flags a file that grew more than 20% since its last daily baseline. None reads the task or checks whether the growth was requested.

Rule 421 matches the word 'and' on a word boundary in the commit subject line, case-insensitively. It inspects no diff and no request. The keyword match selects commits for a person to review but does not say what is wrong, since many single-concern subjects legitimately contain 'and'.

Rule 540 says what is wrong: when an attempted fix fails, its edits must be reverted before delivery, and accumulated dead code from failed fix attempts is forbidden. It names the failure (leftover changes from a discarded attempt) and states the obligation (immediate revert).
